gates.claim: S(e^{i phi}) - S(1) = phi^2 holds THROUGH the branch point -- no feature at phi_0, none at phi_0 +- 1e-5
the identity holds on the whole arc phi in [0, pi], 201 points
S(-1) - S(1) = pi^2 exactly at the endpoint
S is a SYMMETRIC function of the roots -- permuting them changes nothing, which is why a collision (which only permutes) cannot affect it
the elementary symmetric functions are RATIONAL in x by Vieta (e1=(x^2+1)/x, e2=(x^2+x+1)/x, e3=1) hence analytic on the whole arc -- these are the objects a repaired derivation should use

verdict.outcome: The branch point Route 16 found is HARMLESS for S. S(e^{i phi}) - S(1) = phi^2 holds to 4e-40 across the whole arc, including exactly at phi_0 and at phi_0 +- 1e-5.
verdict.why: S sums over ALL roots, so it is symmetric in them. A collision permutes roots; a symmetric function cannot notice a permutation. Only the per-root labelling dies, and only the ARGUMENT used labels.
verdict.what_survives: the transport CONCLUSION S(-1) = S(1) + pi^2. Route 16 never endangered the sum rule; this is the specific reason.
verdict.what_is_still_open: the transport is unproved. It needs a derivation that never names an individual branch. The natural route is the elementary symmetric functions, rational in x by Vieta (G5) and analytic on the whole arc -- and their identities are ALREADY Lean-proved (prod_one_sub_x_mul, prod_x_sub in FiveTwoCyclotomicBloch.lean).
